title: Dominic and the Songbook
premise: Gideon Crane, a former concert pianist turned part-time novelist who keeps his late grandfather's lighthouse and swears the heart is a trainable muscle, is assigned an anonymous pen-pal exchange through his writing group — only to discover his correspondent is Dominic Vale, the rival baker whose lease dispute threatens both their livelihoods on the same harbor street. Their letters, written without names, become the one place each can be honest; when identities are revealed at the winter festival, betrayal and old wounds surface, forcing Gideon to choose between a prestigious publishing contract in the city and staying to fight for Dominic, the bakery, and the found family of the harbor. He chooses belonging: they save the bakery together, co-write a songbook of the town's remembered melodies, and sign the new lease side by side.
about_author: Yara Brightwater is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing coastal oral histories before turning to fiction. She writes love stories set in small working harbors, where memory is a kind of architecture.

chapters.title: The Anonymous Current
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The harbor writing group launches an anonymous pen-pal assignment meant to pair strangers; a clerical error pairs enemies instead. Gideon, guarding his heart after a career-ending injury, begins exchanging letters with someone disarmingly candid about fear and ambition. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity — the first crack in his containment.

chapters.title: Flour and Salt Water
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Letters deepen while daylight rivalry sharpens: Dominic's bakery lease and Gideon's lighthouse funding hinge on the same landlord's decision. Each begins suspecting the truth of who's writing back but keeps writing anyway. Emotional beat: falling in love with an idea of a person while resenting the reality.

chapters.title: Reveal at the Winter Festival
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. At the lantern-lit festival, letters are read aloud anonymously; Gideon realizes mid-reading that Dominic wrote every word, and Dominic watches him understand. Public humiliation, an accusation of manipulation, and the landlord's ultimatum land the same night. Emotional beat: climax — trust shattered exactly when it mattered most.

chapters.title: Every Song Has a Home
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Gideon nearly leaves for the city contract, but finds his grandfather's songbook annotated in Dominic's handwriting — proof of years of quiet devotion. He returns, they rally the harbor to co-sign the bakery lease, and the novel's last scene mirrors its first letter, signed with real names. Emotional beat: resolution — belonging chosen over safety.
